title: HOW MALLARDS MOVE BETWEEN LAND AND WATER

narration_timeline.text: Why do mallard ducks look so different on land and in water, even when ducklings are nearby?
A line of adults glides along the bank, each bird leaving a narrow trail of ripples.
narration_timeline.scene: Adult mallards visibly swimming in a line.

narration_timeline.text: Some ducks step onto the grass to rest, while others keep swimming just beyond the shore.
narration_timeline.scene: Two mallards on grass, then ducks swimming in pond.

narration_timeline.text: On a log, one duck preens its feathers; on the bank, another walks on its broad webbed feet.
narration_timeline.scene: Mallard preening on log, then mallard standing and walking on shoreline.

narration_timeline.text: Away from the water, a pair can settle quietly into the grass between trips.
Then the water draws them back, where smaller groups paddle across the pond at their own pace.
